subject: Starlite integration: inference governance & routing next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@starlitehealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Starlite integration: inference governance & routing next steps

Hi Sanjay / Priya — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

1) Use cases validated
   - Real-time clinician assistant inside the EMR (low-latency; strict PII/PHI controls).
   - Daily batch reranker for patient outreach prioritization (throughput/cost sensitive).
   - Embeddings for historical note search and similarity.

2) Auth & SDK setup
   - Starlite prefers org-wide SSO for engineers (OIDC) for dev/test; production secrets via customer-managed KMS.
   - Action: please confirm whether you can install a short-lived OIDC client for dev or need API-key-based service accounts.

3) Routing & policy guidance (recommended by Redwood)
   - Interactive UI: latency-first routing (primary: rtx-1.2; fallback: mpt-q8n) with max latency 250ms p99.
   - Batch/rerank: cost-first routing (primary: quantized 7B family; fallback: cheaper quantized 4B) with max throughput 10k reqs/hr.
   - Region: pin production traffic to us-west region; cross-region fallback to us-east only on capacity failures.
   - Policy note: automatic fallback chains will preserve output schema but may reduce quality — we'd add a versioned model-label to responses so your app can detect fallback events.

4) Structured output & tool calling
   - We recommend using Redwood's structured-output schema for the med-summary tool (fields: diagnosis, recommended_actions, evidence_refs).
   - Need to confirm whether Starlite will allow outbound calls to our tool endpoint or prefers an internal tool-call adapter.

5) Embeddings & rerankers
   - Plan: host a vector index in your VPC (preferred) or use Redwood-hosted index with encrypted-at-rest option.
   - For reranking we'll return top-k candidate ids + confidence scores; we should sync on the scoring threshold.

Next steps (owner in parentheses):
   - Sanjay: confirm SSO vs service account approach and any network egress constraints (by 2027-10-13).
   - Marcus: send a concise routing/policy proposal + diagram and a sandbox access checklist (attached).
   - Lauren: schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive if Starlite wants to run a quick proof-of-concept (POC).

Attachments: starlite-ma-nextsteps.pdf (summary + checklist), routing-diagram.v1.png (recommended flow).

Thanks — I'll be ready to spin up a sandbox as soon as you confirm auth approach.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@starlitehealth.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya@starlitehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Starlite integration: inference governance & routing next steps

Marcus — really appreciate the detailed recap. Quick answers from our side: 

- Auth: we prefer OIDC for developer access. For production service calls, we require short-lived tokens minted by our internal auth service; we cannot embed long-lived API keys in the app. We can provide a service-account flow that exchanges a signed JWT for short-lived tokens.
- PHI/regulatory: Starlite must keep PHI inside US regions. We can allow cross-region fallback to us-east only for short periods and with encryption-in-transit + audit logs.
- KMS: we will use our AWS KMS in the VPC for production keys.
- Dedicated capacity: procurement will likely request an estimate for a dedicated pool in us-west — can you get a rough committed throughput/price estimate? (cc: Priya for procurement).

We can do the technical deep-dive next week. 2027-10-14 or 2027-10-15 morning PST work for our infra lead.

Thanks,
Sanjay
VP, Platform Engineering
Starlite Health
From: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>

On Mon, Oct 11, 2027 at 3:10 PM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> (recap)

Thanks — adding a few technical clarifications and a draft policy snippet below that we can present to Starlite at the deep-dive. Will keep it high-level in the call, but include the exact config text in the follow-up doc.

Key clarifications:
 - For the short-lived token requirement, Redwood supports an OIDC token-exchange flow and can accept your internal broker as long as the broker mints tokens with the expected audience and scope. We'll need the JWKS endpoint and token TTL expectations.
 - For KMS: we'll support an external KMS via our Private deployment connector; we should confirm network peering options.
 - For regional fallbacks: propose a cooldown of 5 minutes between cross-region failovers to limit PHI movement.

Draft policy (example routing profile — present as plain text on the call):

--- routing-profile: starlite-prod-interactive ---
priority: latency
primary_model: rtx-1.2
fallback_chain: [mpt-q8n, small-quant-7b]
region_pin: us-west-2
cross_region_fallback: us-east-1
max_p99_latency_ms: 250
preserve_kv_cache: true
log_fallback_event: true
---

I'll attach a simplified routing-diagram to show primary/fallback paths. Marcus — can you ask procurement to share an expected committed RPS for the POC so we can size dedicated capacity options?

- Lauren
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
